what_its_for: Fesoterodine is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce symptoms like needing to urinate very urgently, urinating too often, and accidentally leaking urine (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so it can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, chew, or split the tablet. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 4 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 8 mg once daily if needed and if you are tolerating the medication well. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fesoterodine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from moisture and heat. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it may increase dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid activities that require you to be fully alert, such as driving or operating heavy machinery, until you know how this medication affects you. Try to stay cool and drink enough fluids, as fesoterodine can reduce sweating and make it harder for your body to cool down in hot weather. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL other medications you take, especially antifungal medicines like ketoconazole or antibiotics like clarithromycin, as they can increase the level of fesoterodine in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: difficulty urinating or cannot urinate at all, severe constipation or stomach pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing, confusion or hallucinations, painful or difficult urination (which could signal a urinary tract infection), or blurred vision with eye pain or redness (which could be a sign of increased eye pressure).
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your bladder symptoms within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking fesoterodine. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to side effects like confusion, dizziness, and constipation. Use with caution and report any new or worsening symptoms to your doctor. Kidney or liver problems: If you have severe kidney or liver disease, your doctor may keep you on a lower dose of 4 mg and not increase it further. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney or liver problems before starting this medication. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of fesoterodine during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known, so your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits with you.
